# About this book {.unnumbered}

This web-book goes with MEDC 30504, Tissues, Cells & Organ Physiology. Each chapter follows a lecture in the course, uses the course's terms and symbols, and links to the course simulators where one fits.

It covers the cardiovascular and pulmonary blocks, with the muscle lectures and the excitable-cell material that the muscle and autonomic lectures need.

::: {.callout-note title="How AI was used to make this book"}
This book was built with generative AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code) under faculty direction. The AI was used to:

- reformat and rewrite content from the course's earlier web-book, and to draft chapters from the current lectures, lecture notes and small-group materials;
- edit the chapters for accuracy and for consistency with the current course materials, terms and corrections;
- redraw figures, either from equations and the course simulators' models or as adaptations of published figures, which are credited in their captions.

The course faculty set the scope and the conventions, and decided every correction. AI can make mistakes. If something here disagrees with your lectures or looks wrong, tell the course directors.
:::

## How to use it

Read a chapter before or after its lecture. Each one opens with goals and ends with practice questions and the key equations. Boxes marked "Background" hold material you will not be examined on.

The course exams use single-best-answer questions in the NBME style. Most give a short clinical or laboratory scenario and ask you to predict a change or explain its mechanism. The practice questions at the end of each chapter are open-ended instead, so you work through the reasoning rather than pick from a list.

## Sources and figures

Every chapter lists its sources. Every figure was drawn for this book. Figures that redraw a classic experiment or a textbook figure say "adapted from" and cite the original. Figures from openly licensed books keep their license and credit.

## Corrections

If you find an error, tell the course directors.
